 1d - Aerostatics Energy Budget Calculations (Heat Transfer):
For initial pre-heat - taking Sunship from ambient internal temp to operating temp.

Estimated Metrics:
Sunship length: 300m
VS = 1.62, VE = 53%
Volume: 7,492,698.48 m3
Target temperature: 500℃ (Ambient air = 20℃). 𝚫T = 480K
Air density: 1.2 kg/m3
Specific heat (cp)of air: 1005 J/kg݀݀ · K
Mass of air: 8,991,238 kg

…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
Energy calculation:

Sensible heat equation: Q = m cp 𝚫T
Q = 8,991,238 kg · 1005 J/kg · 480K = 4.337TJ (+ 10% ‘losses’ for margin = 4.771 TJ)
4.771 TJ = 1.325 GWh
…………………………………………………………………………………………………
Power calculation:

Desired heating time: 12 hours (slow) = 43,200 seconds, or 6 hours (fast) = 21,600 seconds.
P=Q/t

= 4.771 TJ / 43,200 = 110.43MW for 12 hours, or 221 MW for 6 hours.

…………………………………………………………………………………………………

 Industrial feasibility.
 Power levels in the range of hundreds of MW over 6-12 hours are entirely feasible by current standards, being comparable to the continuous electrical or thermal demand of a small-to-medium industrial facility (e.g. chemical processing, metals, cement, paper, or data centre infrastructure), of which tens of thousands already operate worldwide.

 Much less power is needed for a ‘top-up’, during cargo exchange, while the Sunship is already at or near, true neutral, or optimum negative buoyancy. Each Sunship rarely needs to be fully heated from ambient temperature during its 20 year service life. It is mostly very hot, close to the temperature required for neutral buoyancy, regularly ‘topping up’ the latent heat energy.

 Sustainable energy feasibility.
 The power scale is well within the demonstrated operating envelope of current commercially available sustainable thermal energy systems, such as those developed by Rondo
Energy, or Antora Energy, which are explicitly designed to deliver hundreds of megawatts of dispatchable industrial heat. Consequently, both the timing, magnitude, and delivery method of the Sunship’s required heat input are consistent with existing, scalable, and sustainable industrial technology.

 2a - Aerodynamics Power / Fuel Calculations Per Trip:

Estimated Metrics:
Sunship length: 300m
VS = 1.62, VE = 53%
Estimated Cd: 0.05 (aerodynamic mode - smart tail extended)
Air density (Rho): 1.225 kg/m3
Frontal area: 60,000 m2 (estimated)
Speed: 120 km/h (33.33 m/s)
Trip distance: 10,000 km
Estimated Vogel exponent: 0.4 (Power scales with v2.6 instead of v3)
Hydrogen fuel cell efficiency: 60%

Drag Equation:
 D = ½⍴ · Cd · A · v2
Effective Power Equation:
 P ~ v3 - Vogel (or: effective P = ½⍴ · Cd · A · v3 - V)
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
Baseline Per-Trip Power Calculation (Cd = 0.05, Vogel exponent = 0.4):

 P = ½⍴ · Cd · A · v2.6 = (0.6125 x 0.05 x 60,000) x (33.333 - 0.4) = 16.74 MW
 (16.74 MW = 22,400 total Horsepower, or ~224 horsepower per motor, with 100 propellers total, 50 per side.)

…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………

 As the Cd increases the power requirement follows, to 33.46 MW if Cd doubles to 0.1, increasing drastically to 157.29 MW if Cd = 0.47 (standard reference for a spherical body).
 If the Cd decreases (in line with historical precedents) the power requirement drops to
15.06 MW if Cd = 0.045 (as per TC-6 Airship), or 7.69 MW if Cd = 0.023 (as per Navy Las Angeles
Airship).

 This illustrates the vital importance of the Smart Tail system to reduce the Cd drastically by altering the flow profile towards the idealised teardrop shape, reducing separation.

………………………………………………………………………………………………………………….

 If the Vogel exponent decreases to 0.3 or below, the power requirement jumps to:
23.76 MW, if P ~ v2.7 (Vogel exponent 0.3), or 68 MW if P ~ v3 (Vogel exponent 0).
 If the Vogel exponent increases to 0.5, or 0.6, the power requirement drops to:
11.78 MW, if P ~ v2.5 (Vogel exponent 0.5), or 8.29 MW if P ~ v2.4 (Vogel exponent 0.6)

 This illustrates the vital importance of the BLI integrated drag reduction to convert potential pressure drag into thrust, and the value of the Vogel exponent to encode the overall performance into the calculations simply. The values will of course be updated empirically over time - keeping in mind that, due to Reynolds number, they cannot ever be perfectly predicted or measured until the Sunship is at full operating size

Baseline Per-Trip Energy and Effective Energy Calculations:

Baseline Energy = P · t
(10,000 km @ 120 km/h = 83.33 hours)
= 16.74MW x 83.33
= 1,394.9 MWh (1,394,860 kWh)

…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………...

Per Trip Fuel Calculation:

kg = Baseline Energy / (33.33 kWh/kg @ 60% efficiency)
= 1,394,860 kWh / 19.99 kWh/kg
= 69,777 kg = 70 tonnes H2 (per 10,000km trip @ 120 km/h)

…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………...

Total fuel + storage systems weight

Using an effective power to weight ratio of 4 kWh/kg (including a storage system efficiency of 20%)
the total weight of the H2 fuel plus its storage systems totals to around 350t. There is of course great room to reduce weight here if possible over time as H2 technology improves.
 For comparison, a large cargo ship may burn 1-300 tonnes of fuel per day.

 Feasibility
 At this scale, 16.74 MW of power, needing 70 tonnes of H2, and around 350t of total weight, is around 6% of the standard 300m length Sunship’s ~5600 tonnes gross lift budget. The entire weight of the Sunship is estimated at around 840 tonnes, so roughly 500 tonnes for materials and all other systems + 350t H2 and storage. Changes in component or materials weight are linear and marginal compared to the exponential net lift at this scale, so small to moderate margin of error across core assumptions does not drastically impact feasibility.

 Lowering the average airspeed can drastically improve total Hydrogen and storage system weight requirements. 120 km/h is used as an ambitious but reasonable target, with a Sunship fleet still able to perform huge and valuable total work at lower average airspeeds (e.g. 90-120km/h - around the cruising speed of the Hindenburg some 100 years ago.)
 Raising the average airspeed may also be possible, but the average airspeed may not be able to increase much more, perhaps with a theoretical maximum of around 160 km/h (44.44 m/s).
 While keeping the Cd and Vogel exponent the same, this 33% higher airspeed would require a total Hydrogen fuel weight of 111t per Sunship per trip, and total fuel + systems weight of around 550t, an increase of over 50%.
 This increased average airspeed calculation however with a slightly raised Vogel exponent
(of only 2.7 instead of 2.6) = 162t of H2 per Sunship per trip, and 807t total fuel + systems weight, over double the necessary weight of 120 km/h average airspeed. Potentially beyond the limits of feasibility.

 2b - Maximum Total Green Hydrogen Energy Budget Calculations:

Estimated Metrics:
Fleet size: 25,000 Sunships (ASaaS fleet) / 30,000 ‘Cloudchaser’ XL Sunships (AWC fleet).
Sunship length: 300m / 330m
Average Airspeed: 120 km/h (33.33 m/s)
H2 per Trip: 70 tonnes H2 / 3.04 tonnes H2
Average trip distance: 10,000 km / 400km
Average trip time: 4.32 days / 6 hours
Trips per year (per Sunship): 84.47 / 1183
Sunship utilization: 81%
Total fleet work: 139 Tr ton-km/year (ASaaS) / 142 Tr ton-km/year (AWC)
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………

 Total fleet H2 calculation:

 Total fleet H2 = H2 per trip x trips per year per Sunship x number of Sunships
 Total ASaaS Fleet H2 = 70 x 84.47 x 25,000 = 148 Mt / year
 Total AWC fleet H2 = 3.04 x 1183 x 30,000 = 108 Mt / year

 Total Maximum Global Fleet Hydrogen Requirement = 256 Mt / year

 Due to the short max cycle distance (around 400km), the water collecting Sunships are far more ton-km/year efficient and fuel efficient than the long distance cargo fleet.

 Feasibility:
 Nothing in physics or industrial capacity prevents reaching 260+ Mt/year (or greatly more)
of global green H2 production, within the 21st century, if the demand exists. The world already produces ~100Mt/year of H2 today, most of which is not green Hydrogen. There are engineering, economic, political challenges etc. but no impossibilities - especially if stable Airshipping and AWC industry demand helps drive green H2 production.
 Examples:
 Global oil production: 4,400 Mt/year.
 Global coal production: 8,000 Mt/year.
 Global steel: 1,800 Mt/year.

 Relative to other sectors, the necessary amount of fuel production is modest. Especially if the H2 powered global airship fleet ALSO avoids 1 billion tonnes/year of CO2 emissions.
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………

 Maximum Fleet Size Global Electrolysis Energy Requirements:

 Electrolysis energy input: ~50 kWh per kg H2
 50 kWh per kg H2 = 50MWh / t
 50 x 256,000,000 = 12.8PWh

 Feasibility:
 By mid-century, global energy system modelling consistently indicates total annual electricity production in the hundreds of petawatt-hours, with some long-range scenarios extending toward the ~1,000 PWh/year scale as renewable generation, storage, and transmission mature. In such a context, industrial-scale renewable energy—delivered via standardised solar, wind, storage, and power-electronics infrastructure—becomes the dominant global energy backbone. Against this backdrop, allocating ~13 PWh/year to produce ~260Mt/year of green
Hydrogen, to the global Airship fleet seems very feasible.

 3a - Maximum Atmospheric Water Collection Calculations:
 Exploring the maximum global limits of sustainable fresh water harvesting. An optimistic throughput ceiling analysis, assuming sustained full-payload atmospheric water capture per cycle.

Estimated Metrics:
Global groundwater depletion target: 200-300km3/year (200,000-300,000 Mt/year), or
0.54-0.82km3/day (540-820 Mt/day)
Target as % of global annual hydrological cycle: 0.06% (Replenished via evaporation)
Sunship fleet size: 25,000 over-ocean ‘cloud chaser’ water collecting Sunships.
Sunship length and temperature: 300metres @ 500℃
Sunship payload: 4767t
Max trip distance: ~400km per cycle

 Cycle Time Cycles/Day t/Ship/Day Fleet Mt/day % target offset

 6 hours 4 19,068 476 58-88%

 5 hours 4.8 22,881 572 70-106%

 4 hours 6 28,602 715 87-132%

Modest increases to both the average Sunship length and total fleet size drastically strengthen the results:

Estimated Metrics:
Global groundwater depletion target: 200-300km3/year (200,000-300,000 Mt/year), or
0.54-0.82km3/day (540-820 Mt/day)
Sunship fleet size: 30,000 extra large over-ocean ‘cloud chaser’ water collecting Sunships
Sunship length and temperature: 350 metres @ 500℃
Sunship payload: 7982.9t

 Cycle Time Cycles/Day t/Ship/Day Fleet Mt/day % target offset

 6 hours 4 31,932 958 117-177%

 5 hours 4.8 38,318 1150 140-212%

 4 hours 6 47,897 1437 175-266%

 Feasibility:
 It appears feasible, despite being audacious in scale, to collect a profoundly meaningful amount of atmospheric fresh water with a fleet of 25,000-30,000 standard or extra large specialty
Sunships. Even if the collected water amounts per cycle are reduced from maximum, due to intermittent rain availability, or increased journey distance (leading to increased cycle time).
 When % target offset = over 100%, the collected fresh water can match total global non-renewable groundwater depletion and can begin to replenish key aquifers. This is a very meaningful technological possibility. Sunship technology can directly contribute to a hydrologically sustainable planet, in conjunction with vast improvements in water use efficiency.

 3b - Solar Energy Collection Calculations:

Example inputs:
Sunship length: 300m
Total surface area (approx): 220,000 m2
Solar collection area: 50,000 m2
Solar panel tech: Si structural solar cell (e.g. Praxis Solar)
Solar panel specs: 1 kg/m2, 0.4mm thickness, 24% efficiency
Total Solar panel weight: 50t
Peak solar irradiance: 1000 W/m2
Curvature / orientation / day-night averaging factor: 0.3
Additional losses factor: 0.9

…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
Power calculations:

1000 x 0.24 x 0.3 x 0.9 = 64.8 W/m2
64.8 x 50,000m2 = 3.24MW average continuous power
3.24MW x 24 = 77.76 MWh / day
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
Solar energy budget:
Smart heating (topping up lost heat): ~20-30 MWh/day (~2.5-5% daily heat losses)
Smart vents (airflows, pumps, vents, fans): ~10-20 MWh/day
Core avionics + ‘brain’ (sensors, computers, navigation & comms etc.): ~ 1-2MWh/day
Other systems: ~4-10 MWh/day

Total = 35 - 62 MWh/day
45 - 80% of available solar energy.

Feasibility:
 Despite large assumptions about the surface area and chosen technology of solar panelling, and the total and peak power usage of internal systems - there appears to be no hard limit preventing all of the Sunship’s systems (apart from thrust generation) from being powered by renewable solar energy.

==============================================================================
## EAS FLEET CALCULATOR — WORKED EXAMPLES
==============================================================================

The live calculator is at https://calc.electricairshipping.com — it takes any 3D
shape, measures VS and VE, sizes and flies it, builds a fleet from it, and reports
the economics. Every assumption is visible and changeable by the user.

HOW TO READ THESE. Each block is a real output of the calculator at a chosen
operating point. They are **not forecasts**. They are what the model returns when
you set the levers a particular way, given the assumptions in the papers above.
Two things a careful reader should hold onto:

- The revenue and margin figures are large because the model prices a service that
  does not exist yet at a rate between ocean and air freight, and because operating
  cost is dominated by energy while lift itself is free once the air is hot. They
  describe what the *system* would produce at that scale under stated assumptions,
  not a company's projected accounts.
- Every figure below is calculated or assumed. None is measured. The Sunship is at
  TRL 3 and has not flown.

The four scenarios below span four orders of magnitude — 9 airships to 23,569 — and
are internally consistent: in each case, work ÷ fleet ÷ payload ÷ airspeed returns
the stated utilisation to within 1%.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
